{{< include ../exercise-header.qmd >}}

The elevations in the simulated topographic map below are given in meters. Negative elevations indicate depth below sea level. (The latitudes and longitudes are in "minutes," that is, 1/60th of a degree.)
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| label: C09-zcrhs
f <- mosaicCalc::doodle_fun(~ x & y, seed = 8932)
Pts <- tibble::tribble(
  ~ x, ~y, ~ label,
  39.75, 46.6, "A",
  43.3, 46, "B",
  36.3, 41.7, "C")
contour_plot(
  20*f(x = longitude-37, y = latitude-44) - 100 ~ longitude & latitude,
  domain(longitude = 30:44, latitude = 37:51), 
  contours_at = c(-75, -50, -25,  0.1, 0, 25, 50, 100, 150, 200, 250)) |>
  contour_plot(
    20*f(x = longitude-37, y = latitude-44) - 100 ~ longitude & latitude,
    domain(longitude = 30:44, latitude = 37:51), 
    contours_at = 0, contour_color = "red") |>
  gf_text(y ~ x, label = ~ label, data = Pts, inherit = FALSE)
  
```

1. One of the contours is colored red. What geographic feature does this contour mark? [Coastline]

2. Is this one island or two nearby islands? [One]

3. Which of the marked points is on the most gently sloping beach? [B]
